newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures firmer, others mixed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures firmer, others mixed.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended a day of lacklustre trade firmer on Monday, buoyed by stronger spot gold prices, while other precious metal futures were mixed as the yen's slight rise capped prices, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from flat to 11 yen per gram firmer, with benchmark December up two yen at 1,325 yen.
Private investors, subdued by static prices, generally retreated to the sidelines amid uncertainty over the currency market.
Spot gold was quoted weaker at $358.25/75 per ounce at 0733 GMT, against $358.80/359.30 in New York on Friday.
In the bullion market, spot gold had been stuck within tight ranges during Asian hours.

"Spot gold may consolidate at around the current levels in the near-term, as the market may mark time after the recent steep falls," one trader said. "But the resistance at $360 per ounce would be hard to breach as the fundamental tone is still bearish," he said.
Lingering fears of central bank gold sales continued to cast a shadow on the market.
Platinum futures ranged from three yen per gram lower to one firmer, with benchmark December down two yen at 1,340 yen.
Uncertainty over Russian supplies of platinum group metals, combined with strong demand from the autocatalyst sector continued to provide support to palladium prices.

"The domestic palladium market is gradually becoming tighter, while the platinum market has been less affected by the Russian factor, as South Africa is also a main producer of platinum," one trader said.
Benchmark December palladium was up one yen at 449 yen.
Benchmark December silver was down 0.4 yen per 10 grams at 178.2 yen.
